newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Tsingtao brewery to restructure.
newsitem.headline: China's Tsingtao brewery to restructure.

text.p: China'see Tsingtao Brewery Co Ltd said on Wednesday a holding firm had been formed to hold the listed company in a corporate restructuring.
Tsingtao Brewery Group Co Ltd, the group, had been formed in the northeastern Chinese city of Qingdao to hold Tsingtao Brewery Co Ltd, the company, a spokeswoman for the company told Reuters.

"The company will take this opportunity to restructure its own assets, to make use of preferential treatment given by the government and to implement various merging and acquisition projects," the company said in a statement.
"The company will further enhance its strengths to create a profitable future," it said.
Company chairman Li Guirong said in the statement that assets retructuring was still underway.
"Since the group is newly formed, assets restructuring is still under way. However, it will definitely provide a good opportunity for the growth of the company," he said.

"The company will treasure this chance to gradually move away from its non-principal businesses and inject more valuable assets into the company. We believe that these measures can reinforce the foundation of the company," he said.

"The group will diversify its business in the near future. Excessive personnel will be redistributed in order to lessen the burden of the company. Resources will be reallocated optimally to achieve economies of scale," he said.
Li said he believed the group and the company would be mutually beneficial and their success was "foreseeable".

The company also said it expected the disposal of non-principal activities, the redistribution of excess staff, the injection of valuable assets, merger and acquisition projects, and the beneficial treatment offered by the Chinese government would provide it with a profitable future.
Some of the offices in its 19-storey Tsingtao Beer Mansion in Qingdao will be leased out, it said. "It will become a stable income source of the company in the future," the statement said.
Tsingtao Brewery Co Ltd owns six breweries in China.
